newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Thursday with market sentiment dampened by an official crackdown on the stock markets, traders said.
But the annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 12.0 percent from 11.5 percent on Thursday, supported by a large number of new A share issues this week, they said.
Total turnover on the six-contract market rose to 9.6 million lots from 7.8 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Beijing on Wednesday announced a ban on speculative trading by state enterprises on the stock markets, the latest of a series of official measures to cool down overheated stock trading. The crackdown made China's share prices plunge on Thursday.
"The plunge on the stock market made many institutions liquidate their positions on the repo markets today, depressing the repo rates," one trader said.
But a dozen new A share issues this week supported the repo rates to some extent, expecially the seven-day contract.
Traders said they expected the contracts to consolidate on Friday, waiting for further market-moving news.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Thursday on a continued liquidity outflow due to the heavy schedule of new A share issues, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 120.48 yuan from 120.85 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 918,726 lots from 1.1 million lots.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to rebound shortly with trading on the stock markets cooling down.
